# /pipeline — {{ spec.name }} Pipeline Orchestrator

This is the entry point for the weekly research pipeline in {{ spec.name }}.
It delegates all orchestration to the framework command `research_framework pipeline`,
which sequences collect → extract → scout → [human triage] → research → verify →
report against the vault's spec.

**You are a shim.** For each mode below, shell out to the framework command and
display its output verbatim. Do not reimplement pipeline logic here.

## Resolving the vault

Every command below takes the vault root as its first argument, written as
`"${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}"`. Run the commands verbatim — from the vault, or with
`VAULT_DIR` exported — and do NOT substitute a literal path. This file travels
with the vault: it is committed to the vault's own repository and cloned onto
other machines, so a path resolved at render time would name a directory that
no longer exists by the time an agent reads it.

## Modes

| Mode | Framework command | Stops for human? |
|------|-------------------|-----------------|
| `full` | `research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" full` | Yes — after scout |
| `collect` | `research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" collect` | No |
| `extract` | `research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" extract` | No |
| `scout` | `research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" scout` | Yes — at triage |
| `resume` | `research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" resume` | No |
| `finish` | `research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" finish` | No |
| `status` | `research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" status` | No |

### `/pipeline full`

Shell out to:

    research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" full

Print the output verbatim. The framework runs collect → extract → scout in
sequence, then stops with a triage prompt. When ready, run `/pipeline resume`.

### `/pipeline collect`

    research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" collect

Runs Phase 1 collection scripts. No AI involved.

### `/pipeline extract`

    research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" extract

Runs Phase 2 extraction against `_pipeline/raw/`.

### `/pipeline scout`

    research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" scout

Runs Phase 3 scouting from the context tree. Stops at the triage prompt.

Triage happens in `_pipeline/scout-report.json`, under `topics_found.new` — a
pipeline run writes no Topic Radar note (that is a cycle-orchestrator artifact;
see `ARCHITECTURE.md` § "The triage checkpoint"). `/pipeline resume` researches
every entry in that list in one pass; to defer one, delete its entry before
resuming.

### `/pipeline resume`

    research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" resume

Continues after human triage: research → verify → report. The `research` stage
here is NOT the `/research` slash command — it is the headless runner stage,
which takes its queue from `_pipeline/scout-report.json` (see `ARCHITECTURE.md`
§ "The two research entry points"). All three stages run
headlessly: `research` dispatches the note-writer prompt built from the
approved topics, `verify` grades the corpus, `report` writes the briefing. The
run needs no further input — do not stop to ask questions, and do not fall back
to researching by hand.

### `/pipeline finish`

    research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" finish

Runs verify → report only (skips research if queue already clear).

### `/pipeline status`

    research_framework pipeline "${VAULT_DIR:-$PWD}" status

Prints the current `_pipeline/pipeline-state.json` as a structured summary.
Read-only — invokes no agent.

## Why a shim?

The orchestration logic lived inline in this file in earlier vault versions
(~410 lines). It now lives in the framework so improvements propagate to every
vault without manual porting.

To deviate locally from the framework version, create
`.claude/commands/pipeline.local.md` — Claude Code resolves the local override
first. The existing 410-line prose can serve as the body of that local override.

## State file

The framework writes `_pipeline/pipeline-state.json` between phases. Use
`/pipeline status` to inspect it without running anything. To restart from
scratch, delete the state file and run `/pipeline full`.

## Arguments

$ARGUMENTS
